# Kyoto Family Trip Plan for 10–13 April 2026

A relaxed 4-day Kyoto itinerary for **2 adults + 1 child**, built around temples, easy walks, local food, and one kid-friendly museum. It keeps you to **one hotel base** for the whole trip and targets the **180,000 JPY** budget excluding international flights.

## 4-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget

| Day | Plan | Estimated transport | Estimated meals | Estimated total |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Day 1 · Fri 10 Apr | Kyoto Station, Higashi Hongan-ji, Kyoto Tower area, Gion evening stroll | 2,000 JPY | 10,000 JPY | 12,000 JPY |
| Day 2 · Sat 11 Apr | Arashiyama bamboo grove, Tenryu-ji, riverside walk, monkey park if energy allows | 4,500 JPY | 11,500 JPY | 16,000 JPY |
| Day 3 · Sun 12 Apr | Fushimi Inari early visit, Nishiki Market lunch, Kyoto Railway Museum | 3,500 JPY | 12,500 JPY | 16,000 JPY |
| Day 4 · Mon 13 Apr | Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka/Ninenzaka easy walk, souvenir time, departure buffer | 2,500 JPY | 9,000 JPY | 11,500 JPY |

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Family Itinerary

### Day 1: Easy arrival and Gion evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Arrive, check in, and keep the first day light with a short walk around **Kyoto Station** and nearby areas.
- Afternoon: Visit **Higashi Hongan-ji** for a calm temple start; it is spacious and easy with a child.
- Evening: Walk through **Gion** and the nearby streets for a gentle first taste of Kyoto.
- Food: Try a simple **udon set**, tofu dishes, or a family-friendly izakaya near Kyoto Station.

Estimated spend:
- Transport: **2,000 JPY**
- Meals: **10,000 JPY**
- Total: **12,000 JPY**

### Day 2: Arashiyama temples and riverside walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- Morning: Head early to **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** before crowds build up.
- Afternoon: Visit **Tenryu-ji** and enjoy the garden, then take a slow riverside walk.
- Late afternoon: If everyone still has energy, do the short climb to the **Iwatayama Monkey Park**; skip it if the child is tired.
- Food: Have **yudofu**, soba, or a riverside lunch with simple set meals.

Estimated spend:
- Transport: **4,500 JPY**
- Meals: **11,500 JPY**
- Total: **16,000 JPY**

### Day 3: Fushimi Inari and the railway museum
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/train-front.svg
- Morning: Go early to **Fushimi Inari Taisha** and do a partial climb only; turn back when the child wants a break.
- Afternoon: Stop at **Nishiki Market** for shared snacks and lunch.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Afternoon: Stop at **Nishiki Market** for shared snacks and lunch, Kyoto, Japan
- Late afternoon: Visit the **Kyoto Railway Museum**, the best kid-friendly museum in this plan.
- Food: Share market bites such as tamagoyaki, croquettes, grilled skewers, and sweets.

Estimated spend:
- Transport: **3,500 JPY**
- Meals: **12,500 JPY**
- Total: **16,000 JPY**

### Day 4: Kiyomizu-dera and old Kyoto streets
- Morning: Visit **Kiyomizu-dera** early for cooler crowds and easier photos.
- Afternoon: Walk slowly through **Sannenzaka** and **Ninenzaka**, with plenty of snack and shopping stops.
- Evening: Return to the hotel, collect luggage, and head to your departure point.
- Food: Choose a final Kyoto meal of **tofu**, **tempura**, or a family set meal near the temple area.

Estimated spend:
- Transport: **2,500 JPY**
- Meals: **9,000 JPY**
- Total: **11,500 JPY**

## Budget Fit for the Whole Trip

| Category | Estimated cost |
|---|---:|
| Hotel, 3 nights | 78,000 JPY |
| Transport in Kyoto | 12,500 JPY |
| Meals and snacks | 43,000 JPY |
| Temple/museum entries | 9,000 JPY |
| Local shopping and buffer | 18,000 JPY |
| Total | **160,500 JPY** |

### Budget notes
- This leaves about **19,500 JPY** as a cushion for taxi rides, extra snacks, or higher meal prices.
- A **single hotel base near Kyoto Station** or on the Karasuma side keeps transit simple and avoids hotel changes.
- If you want to save more, reduce taxi use and rely on buses/subway plus one or two short walks.

## Packing Checklist for Kyoto in April

- Light jacket or cardigan for cool mornings and evenings
- Comfortable walking shoes for temple paths and stone streets
- Compact umbrella or packable rain jacket
- Layers for changing spring temperatures
- Small day bag for water, snacks, tissues, and souvenirs
- Portable charger and charging cables
- IC card or transit card wallet
- Cash in yen for small shops, markets, and temple fees
- Child essentials: snacks, wipes, spare shirt, small activity item
- Sun protection: hat, sunscreen, sunglasses
- A foldable tote for market purchases
- Any medication and basic first-aid items
